messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: p99 streaming tail latency > SLO in eu-west-2 (service: streaming-api). Alert started 2026-03-14T09:00:54Z :rotating_light:

alex: ack, I'm on it. - checking dashboards and kube events

alex: p95 backends up ~350ms but p99 is 2.8s for streaming appenders, error rate for streaming connections up 1.6% (baseline ~0.01%).

sara: seeing TLS handshake spikes in eu-west-2-azb -> azc path on tcp metrics. SYN RTTs jump, retransmits up.

ryan: also high DNS lookup latencies from pods in azb. `dig` from a repro pod shows ~200-400ms on some names intermittently.

jess: confirming customer impact: a subset of websocket sessions are stalling at the initial handshake and during rekeys. 5 customer tenants showing reconnect cascades. Adding to incident board.

alex: initial suspect: cross-AZ VPC routing asymmetry after a routing change earlier this morning? I see a config commit to the egress route table at 07:18. Pulling netflow now.

maya: @alex grabbing NAT gateway metrics — ephemeral port usage at 92% for the primary nat-gw in azb. Could be port exhaustion causing connection resets & retries that translate into TLS handshake/backoff.

ops-oncall: rolling CGW logs show `connection reset by peer` and `long SYN wait (handshake > 1s)` clustered around the same times as p99 spikes.

alex: running quick check: `kubectl exec -n streaming -c probe pod/probe-01 -- curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/health` shows repeated `TCP handshake timeout` intermittently.

sara: packet captures from a traceroute show packetloss ~1.2% between azb nat-subnet and azc transit. Looks like selective retransmits on established flows.

ryan: DNS caches on our resolver pods show TTL expiry floods; upstream resolver in azb has elevated query queue length. Might be a hot-spot routing through azb resolver instance.

alex: mitigation plan attempt 1 — fail traffic off the saturated nat-gw in azb to the standby nat-gw in azc. Doing a controlled route preference flip for streaming-instances in azb. Will monitor p99.

incident-bot: Action taken: updated route table rtb-XXX to prefer nat-gw-standby in azc for tag=streaming (runbook: crosszone-egress-fallback)

maya: after route flip p99 dropped to 1.1s within 3min, streaming stalls decreased. Error rate down to 0.4%. Good sign.

jess: can we confirm no downstream customers lost persistent sessions during the switch? Any reconnect storms?

alex: quick check — reconnects spiked by ~8% momentarily during the reroute but trended back to baseline in ~6 minutes. No long-lived session losses reported in customer SLO telemetry.

maya: follow-up mitigation: request CloudOps to scale nat-gw fleet in eu-west-2 by +2, and enable ephemeral port pool expansion for the primary subnets. Filing ticket NOW (#INC-2026-437).

ops-oncall: noted. Also toggled DNS resolver HA to round-robin across two resolver instances (was single-primary). Propagating change.

sara: adding observation: TLS handshake spikes correspond to bursts of SYN retransmits — we should validate MTU and ECMP hashing after route change.

ryan: rolling a short-lived iptables conntrack wait increase on streaming frontends to reduce premature connection drops: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_synrecv=60` applied to streaming nodes (can revert after).

alex: heading to handoff — need someone to own monitoring until we have root cause. Summary: transient cross-AZ packet loss + NAT ephemeral exhaustion + resolver hotspot caused increased SYN/TLS handshakes and streaming p99 breaches. Primary mitigation: reroute egress away from saturated nat-gw, scale nat fleet, make DNS resolver HA, conntrack tweak.

maya: I'll take oncall. I'll keep the mitigations in place and coordinate with cloud ops for a permanent fix. Next steps: full netflow + BGP diff, NAT capacity review, runbook updates.

jess: customer impact estimate for post-mortem: ~12 minutes of p99 > SLO peak, ~6 minutes of elevated reconnects for ~0.3% of active sessions, 5 tenant incidents escalated to support but auto-recovered.

alex: thanks team. Assigning followups: #1 nat capacity (ryan), #2 DNS resolver HA + runbook (sara), #3 routing commit review (alex).

ops-oncall: paging cleared, transition to monitoring. Will reopen if metrics slide back above thresholds. :white_check_mark:

maya: will produce incident timeline and initial RCA draft by EOD.

jess: add post-incident action: add an automated alert for nat ephemeral usage >85% with prescriptive playbook to scale or reroute.

alex: saved logs + pcap to /incidents/1958007654/artefacts/ for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident update: status=mitigated, severity=sev2, assignee=maya, created_by=incident-bot

maya: handing off to oncall for night watch. Closing thread for triage; will open a postmortem thread once RCA is complete.

ops-oncall: ack, monitoring until 2026-03-14T13:00:00Z then hand back to next shift.
